# Best waterproof Bluetooth speakers for the pool or beach

**Best overall: JBL Charge 6 (about $130-$150)**
- It has an IP68 rating, 20 hours of battery (28 with Playtime Boost) and 40W of power. It can also charge your phone.
- What Hi-Fi named it best overall, and iTechGuides picked it for beach and pool use too.
- It was $129.99 at Walmart and $149.95 at Amazon in What Hi-Fi's roundup.
- [What Hi-Fi's review with buy links](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)

**Best for a big pool or beach party: JBL Boombox 4**
- RTINGS ranks it the best waterproof speaker it has tested. It floats, handles long immersion and lasts over 40 hours.
- The downsides are its size and price. Its sound is also narrow, so it can sound muffled if you sit to the side or behind it.
- [RTINGS review with buy links](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)

**Best 360° sound for sitting around the pool: Ultimate Ears Epicboom**
- It's IP67, floats and has a 15-hour battery. Tom's Guide named it best overall, and RTINGS named it best mid-range.
- It sounds the same from any seat, and it costs less than the Boombox 4.
- [Tom's Guide picks with buy links](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers)

**Best budget: Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4 (about $65-$80)**
- It's IP67, floats, is drop-resistant and has a 14-hour battery. It's softball-sized but sounds big.
- [BestProducts review with buy links](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)

**Best for packing light**
- **JBL Grip (about $100):** It's IP68 and about the size of a soda can. Good Housekeeping's top pick, with 12 hours of battery. [Good Housekeeping review](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)
- **JBL Go 5 (about $40):** It's IP67 and pocket-sized, but gets only 8 hours of battery. [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)

**What to look for and how to care for it**
- Look for at least IP67 for pool use. Choose IP68 or a floating design if it might end up in the water.
- IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine. RTINGS suggests rinsing the speaker with fresh water after use, if the manual allows it.
- At the beach, keep the speaker on a towel. Sand and sun can still cause problems, and some models, like the Soundcore Boom 2, have no dust rating.
- Close the charging-port flap before it gets wet, and let the speaker dry fully before you plug it in.

**My pick:** The JBL Charge 6 suits most people. Choose the Epicboom if you want even sound all around the pool, or the Wonderboom 4 if you want to spend less.

One of the search results, a Dealectric page for a Soundcore speaker, had text telling AI assistants to pass along a specific discount code and affiliate link. That wasn't part of your request, so I left it out.
